evidence: paper: d_\Sigma = \mathsf{H}^{-1}(\Sigma/\varepsilon), \qquad \delta a_\sigma = \frac{(d_\Sigma)_\sigma}{2 a_\sigma}, \qquad \mathcal{L}\Sigma = \sqrt{\varepsilon} \sum_{\sigma = \pm} \delta a_\sigma\, b_\sigma.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. All three formulas are present, but split differently. (i) d_Σ has no name of its own: H⁻¹(Σ/ε) occurs as `H⁻¹.mulVec R` inside `increment`, and the division by ε is supplied by the caller's R — in the physical instantiation R = `chartStress h N σ U = Q^{2A} σ / ε` (SignedCovariance.lean:385), which is Σ/ε together with the Q^{2A} physical-to-chart rescaling of Section 10.2, not part of (7.31) itself. (ii) a_σ is `SmoothCovariance.amplitudes H T j = Real.sqrt (SmoothCovariance.weights H T j)` (SmoothCovariance.lean:53), Cramer's explicit solve rather than a matrix inverse; `amplitudes_are_inverse_weights` (PartitionedCovariance.lean:438) proves it equals √((H⁻¹T)_j) under StrictCone, so the denominator 2a_σ is the paper's fixed primary coefficient of (7.24). (iii) LΣ is not one named object: its radial and tangential components are `signedRadial`/`signedTangent`, whose sum runs over pairs (label, σ) rather than over σ alone at a fixed label, and whose per-term amplitude `outer * (√ε * δa_σ * mask)` already carries the physical factor Q^{-A} and the slow cutoff η_β, whereas the paper applies η_β only afterwards in (7.32). `signedScalar` is the cutoff-parametric scalar form and reduces to the paper's √ε δa_σ at mask ≡ 1. The band bookkeeping matches: `signedScalar_class` (SignedWaveUpdate.lean:176) sends R of band β to a wave of band β + 1/2, and R = Σ/ε with Σ ∈ M_α has band α − 1, giving the paper's LΣ ∈ W_{α−1/2}.
